Issued at 148 AM EDT Tue Aug 4 2026

             -----------Synoptic Overview-----------

Florida's weather continues to be influenced by a weak mid-level low
over Georgia. It has become fully cut off from the jet stream and is
moving very little. Negative surface pressure anomalies immediately
north of Central Florida continue to provide south-southwesterly
background flow over the peninsula. A reservoir of above-normal
total moisture (PWATS > 2") remains overhead.

Over the next couple of days, the disturbance over Georgia will
fill and weaken further as the Bermuda high expands westward toward
the Mid-Atlantic states. Consequently, the surface high-pressure
axis is forecast to quickly move northward during this period,
reaching Central Florida on Wednesday before lifting over the Deep
South by Thursday. This will allow onshore flow to develop from
the Atlantic. In this regime, moisture values may dip slightly
but hold at or just above seasonal norms.

The 03/12Z ensemble suite continues to track an inverted trough
westward and toward the Southeast U.S. by Thursday night or
Friday. Considerable disagreement remains regarding its track and
sharpness as it approaches the coast. Taken together, a surge of
higher moisture should pass near or over Central Florida on Friday
and Saturday.

From Sunday into early next week, cluster analysis shows strong
agreement that the Bermuda high will flatten and stretch westward
over the Gulf and Florida. This would likely nudge the surface
high pressure axis southward, perhaps reaching very close to
our latitude by Monday. Somewhat drier air, associated with an
approaching Saharan Air Layer (SAL), may impinge on South Florida
in about a week.

             -------Sensible Weather & Impacts-------

Today - Tonight...

Offshore flow weakens through the day, but should still be
sufficient to steer storms toward the northeast. It may also push
a few showers toward the I-4 corridor and points northward in the
morning hours. By afternoon, the lighter flow should allow the
Atlantic sea breeze to form and push near or west of I-95 from
Brevard County and points south. Hi-res guidance indicates that
scattered storms and outflows will form over the interior as we
heat up and destabilize by early afternoon. Once this activity
approaches the sea breeze, additional storm development appears
likely along the coast in the mid to late afternoon. Overall,
rain and storm chances should range from 60-70% over the interior
to 70-80% along the coast today.

Wet microbursts producing wind gusts from 40-50 mph will be the
primary hazard, along with frequent lightning. As in past days,
there is a 5-10% chance for 3-4" rainfall amounts, which could
cause some minor flooding in urban and poorly drained locales.

Seasonably hot today with highs in the low 90s and heat indices
from 100-105. Most areas look to dry out tonight, but a few showers
may skirt the Treasure Coast before daybreak.

Wednesday - Thursday...

As high pressure quickly moves northward, a pattern change arrives
in Central Florida. An increasingly dominant Atlantic sea breeze
and onshore flow is expected, shifting the highest rain and storm
chances toward the interior and west coast. Still, we expect a
30-50% chance of showers and storms along the east coast, mainly
in the morning and early afternoon. Interior locations should see
50-70% coverage. Brief gusty winds from 40-50 mph and torrential
rainfall will remain the top concerns with these storms. Highs
should range from the upper 80s beachside to the lower 90s over
the interior.

Friday - Saturday...

By Friday morning, moisture should increase as the easterly wave
(inverted trough) moves toward the state. As mentioned in the
overview, the sharpness and trajectory of the wave will influence
how organized showers and storms will be with this feature. We will
maintain 60-80% rain chances through this period, with activity
most common at the coast in the morning hours before shifting over
the interior. We'll need to monitor trends closely for any training
bands of rainfall, but it's too early to get into these specifics.

Easterly flow will be enhanced during this timeframe, causing choppy
surf and an increased risk of life-threatening rip currents at
our beaches to end the week. Seasonably warm to hot temperatures
remain in the forecast, though it may end up a touch cooler,
especially at the coast due to the brisk onshore flow.

Sunday - Early Next Week...

Guidance largely agrees that the surge of moisture associated with
the aforementioned wave will lift northward and away from Central
and South Florida by Sunday and especially Monday. However,
moisture values should only tick down to near-normal values
for mid-August. With a robust sea breeze circulation expected,
scattered storms (30-60%) should still form each day - with the
greatest coverage over the interior.
